column1: # check-all.sh baseline — CCPR's own expected exit code per shipped check.
# Format: <name>\t<expected-exit>\t<note>  (note is free text, for humans;
# check-all.sh never parses it). Comment lines (#) and blank lines are
# ignored. Tab-separated on purpose (readable and diffable without jq;
# bash 3.2 has no associative arrays, so `IFS=$'\t' read` is the parser).
# This file declares EXPECTATIONS, never commands — the check catalogue
# (name -> which script/args run it) lives once, in check-all.sh itself.
# ONE entry is non-zero BY DESIGN, not a regression: memory-lint.sh's 5
# warnings are long-standing memory-freshness notices. It was two until
# 30.08.2026 -- doc-volume-check.sh now scans only git-tracked files, so the
# oversized files it used to report (all of them untracked working state
# under docs/memory/) are out of its scope and its expected exit is 0.
# Re-measure and update this file DELIBERATELY when a check's expected
# outcome actually changes -- the same "re-measure the pair together, never
# adjust one" discipline CONTRIBUTING.md already asks of the -t . /
# --without-t measurement (WI-0126 lineage). Do not let this file drift
# silently out of step with the tree it describes.
# Measured 30.08.2026 on the working tree of HEAD 666e8e6 plus the check
# changes this line ships with. Two of these entries are now
# environment-independent by construction rather than by luck: memory-lint
# and conformance-run report their own scope, so a machine without those
# targets gets could-not-run instead of a divergence, and doc-volume-check
# measures only what git tracks. Verified in a fresh clone with an empty
# HOME: 0 divergent, 2 could-not-run, everything else match.
